recipes.name: Jen's Chorizo Pasta
ingredients_raw: 5 (4 ounce) links chorizo sausage (such as Johnsonville®)
1 (8 ounce) package button mushrooms, stems trimmed

steps.text: Preheat an outdoor grill for medium heat and lightly oil the grate.

Cook sausages on the preheated grill, turning occasionally, until no longer pink in the center, about 10 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read 160 degrees F (70 degrees C). Cut into bite-sized pieces; set aside.

Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Stir in penne and cook in boiling water until tender yet firm to the bite, about 11 minutes. Drain and set aside.

Meanwhile, melt 1 cup butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook and stir garlic in melted butter until softened and fragrant, about 5 minutes. Stir in cream and red pepper flakes; bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then whisk in Parmesan cheese until melted. Keep sauce warm over low heat, stirring occasionally to keep smooth.

Melt remaining 1 tablespoon butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add onion, red bell pepper, and mushrooms; cook and stir until vegetables are tender. Season with salt and pepper. Stir in chorizo pieces and cook until hot. Combine with penne and Parmesan cream sauce to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Jen's Chorizo Pasta
raw_recipe.description: Spicy chorizo pasta served with a delectable cream sauce.

review.reviewBody: This was an awesome pasta.. But I changed the recipe some what. I bought the chorizo from the meat market down the street. I didn't grill it because chorizo has so much flavor I didn't want to loose it and you will with grilling, so I steamed/water boiled it in a pan. When I pulled the sausage out of the pan I kept all the grease in there and sauteed the onions, bell pepper and mushrooms in the grease.. I didn't use the extra 1 tablespoon butter. It was great! :) My husband really loved it too.

I made a few changes, and this recipe was delicious!
I used Mexican Chorizo, removed casing, cooked it up and set it aside. Trying to reserve as much of the chorizo juice and oil in the pan as I could. Then I added the butter, garlic, and onion, sautéed until garlic was soft, and onion was transparent. I didn't have heavy cream, so I needed to improvise; I used about 4.5oz of cream cheese and a cup of milk, then that combine, then added that then the parmesan cheese. I kept the flame very low and constantly stirred to make sure the milk and cream cheese wasn't being over cooked. I omitted the pepper flakes because honestly, it just didn't need it, because the chorizo was so spicy. I also omitted the mushrooms, as I'm allergic. But I needed a vegetable in there besides the red pepper, so I added a heaping handful of fresh spinach with the chopped red pepper with the rest of the butter. Once pasta was ready I added that to the sauce pan, as well as the chorizo, and combined. I will definitely be making this again. It was very easy, quick, and delicious. Boyfriend loved it as well. :)

Simply the best pasta recipe on Allrecipies for me so far. It was difficult to wait to review after making it twice. I prepared As-Is and it was outstanding! Be sure to drain and soak up all the grease from the chorizo. The next time I made it I modified it to be smoky and with more meat so it was amazing - better than any best restaurant. I added smoked paprika and substituted smoked sea salt along with adding garlic shrimp and shredded grilled chicken. Also added ¼ c cream cheese to sauce and used half & half instead of cream. Topped it with chopped bacon and fresh ground black pepper. Next time I’ll see how it turns out with half the butter and milk, the calories must be ridiculous.

I made this using plant-based chorizo for my vegetarian daughter (browned in skillet, not grilled) and also whole wheat farfalle, using half heavy cream & half oat milk, and the whole family loved it! Will definitely make again!

Excellent. I halved the recipe because it was only the two of us and there was still leftovers. I did halve the butter as some had mentioned here, I also cooked the chorizo in the oven and used some of the drippings when sauteing the vegetables. I removed the casing on the chorizo and crumbled it as the casing was too tough. Will make again for sure!

This a a really great recipe. I used spicy chorizo that we got from our CSA share and used a stove-top grill pan as it is freezing here! I cut back on the butter (using only 1 stick), and I added more cracked red pepper. It was rich without being too greasy. I think 1 cup of butter would be too much. Also, I think whole or low fat milk would work fine instead of heavy cream, but I did use HC this time. It was very yummy and there were lots of left overs. If using spinach wait until the very end to add, or else it will be slimy.

This was very good. I subbed Linguica for chorizo. I also subbed half and half for the heavy cream, used fresh mushrooms and green peppers (all I had). I used a reviewers suggestion and sautéed sausage first rather than grill, removed sausage from pan and sautéed vegetables in pan drippings. A keeper!

As it is written would have been too much butter. I only used one stick of butter. Also cooked mushrooms down in some dry white wine as suggested from another reviewer. Came together great with these changes.

Great recipe that lends itself to a bit of chopping and changing. Used Philadelphia cooking cream instead of straight cream, added some chicken stock and a dash of cooking wine which just lifts everything. Didn't have any peppers so I just folded some spinach leaves in at the end. I forgot the cheese but was still yum. Thank you for a brilliant recipe.
Just make sure YOU fry the chorizo in a pan and save the juice for the rest of vegetables.

Absolutely fantastic!! I removed the chorizo from the casing and cooked it like ground beef. I used the chorizo grease to make the base of the creamy sauce instead of a cup of butter. This is a restaurant-quality meal and very, very easy to make.

This was great, and pretty simple, though my doctor wouldn't be so happy with it {cholesterol, anyone?}. I had raw chorizo sausage and they were larger than the pre-packaged ones, so it was heavy on the chorizo, but tasted terrific. Easy to make adjustments: I didn't have mushrooms and they seemed extraneous {true}, and I had a green pepper instead of red, certainly appropriate for this dish. I recommend slightly undercooking the pasta and combining it all in the pasta pot for a minute or so.
I just used smoked chorizo, par cooked and heated up all the ingredients at the end.
Following up on a previous rating…used 1# Chorizo instead of links….kicks
Halved the meat and increased the veg. Still great

I think I assumed delectable to mean “light” sauce, very thick, like a casserole. I used 1/2 of the butter as others recommended but think I should have cut the Parmesan in half as well. Ended up using 1 and 1/2 cup of whipping cream to thin out a bit, probably should of used 1/2 of milk instead. Great flavor. The aromas are amazing. Boyfriend liked it. Still waiting on the verdict from the kids. A lot of pots to clean.

Picky husband had seconds and so did the kids! Changes- no mushrooms. crumbled sweet italian sausage and crushed red pepper (what I had on hand). I used 2 tsp of the pepper in place of the 1/4c pepper flakes.

I have never reviewed a recipe before but I made this last night and it was solid. I'm not a mushroom guy and I had some jalapenos in my garden that were begging to be used so I substituted. Not because the recipe needed it, just because the jalapenos were calling. I sliced them long ways and thin and it added that flavor I love. I would definitely make this again. oh...and the picture had tortellini in it and I had some so I thought...why not? I used that instead of penne. I was happy with the result.

I reduced the recipe to a portion for two. I used fresh chorizo as called for in the recipe. If you are using pre cooked or smoked chorizo it can be added with the peppers and onions at the end. Any type of pasta will work including linguine. Thanks for a really good recipe.
It was good. Way too much butter. Next time I will do 1/2 the butter.
